M12.01.note: AV conduction can fail at different levels; coronary artery obstruction is a separate concept. Known complete-block examples support separate atrial/ventricular observation only; no conduction-block simulator or exact lesion localization is provided.

M12.02.note: Prolonged PR with every P conducted supports first-degree delay in the underlying rhythm. Approved text does not guarantee normal output or always-narrow QRS; the supplied source example is sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block.

M12.03.note: The classic progressive-PR/nonconducted-P sequence must be checked across enough beats. AV-node location and narrow QRS are common rather than universal. Known source example is qualified; no block mechanism is simulated.

M12.04.note: No verified Mobitz-II or 2:1 specimen is available. The approved 2:1 classification limitation is an explicit explanatory addition, not a reconstructed source figure or an invented diagnosis.

M12.05.note: The approved text corrects the source guaranteed-escape wording: an escape may be slow, unreliable or absent. The known source crop shows one narrow-QRS escape example only; neither narrow QRS nor reliable escape is universal. AV dissociation alone does not establish complete block.

M12.06.note: Unrecorded and unscored feature-comparison checkpoint. First-degree, Mobitz-I and complete-block source examples are available; Mobitz-II/2:1 and unreliable/absent-escape examples are not fabricated. No treatment choice is made.
